key_insight: CHOPPED estimated that child avatar accounts aged 5–12 were shown 25 unhealthy food marketing instances per month during 2-hour daily YouTube viewing, including 24 that were child-targeted.
clinical_relevance: This public-health research may inform monitoring of children’s digital food-marketing exposure, but it does not establish effects on diet or health.
method: Used CHOPPED AI to collect and characterize marketing around YouTube-recommended videos.
Monitored six child and two adult avatar profiles, browsing while signed out, across four Canadian cities for two months.
Compared monthly exposure and child-targeted techniques under 24-hour and 2-hour daily viewing periods.
evidence_signal: Among 60,633 collected marketing instances, the boys’ profile aged 9–12 received significantly more child-targeted unhealthy food marketing than several comparison profiles under 24-hour monitoring, but not under 2-hour daily viewing.
watch_item: Simulated avatar exposure may not reflect children’s actual viewing, and the abstract does not report CHOPPED’s detection accuracy.
paper_title: Unboxing unhealthy food marketing: An analysis of the extent and nature of unhealthy food marketing to children on YouTube in Canada using the CHOPPED artificial intelligence system
